svg.text: FIG 05: SECOND-ORDER RLC NETWORKS & THE 4 DAMPING REGIMES
Canonical 2nd-Order Engine • Series/Parallel Duality Matrix • Over/Critical/Under/Undamped Profiles • Initial Derivatives

g.text: Every 2-energy-storage-element circuit reduces to the canonical 2nd-order ODE:
• α = Neper Frequency (attenuation factor, rad/s or Np/s)
Setting auxiliary equation s² + 2αs + ω₀² = 0 yields the two poles:
1. α² > ω₀² (ζ > 1): Distinct real roots → Overdamped
2. α² = ω₀² (ζ = 1): Repeated real roots → Critically Damped
3. α² < ω₀² (0 < ζ < 1): Complex conjugate roots → Underdamped
Stability Criterion: Real part Re(s₁,₂) = -α must be < 0.
If α < 0 (due to active dependent sources), poles lie in RHP → Unstable blowup!
In the underdamped regime, poles form conjugate pair: s₁,₂ = -α ± jω_d
Quality Factor Q & Damping Ratio ζ:
• Higher Q → Lower damping ζ → More persistent ringing oscillations.
• As R changes from 0 to ∞, poles trace semicircles of radius ω₀!
• Distance of poles from origin is ALWAYS |s| = ω₀!
• Damping angle: cos θ = ζ = α / ω₀.
• In Series RLC: Increasing R INCREASES damping (α ∝ R).
• In Parallel RLC: Increasing R DECREASES damping (α ∝ 1/R)!
Open circuit R = ∞ in Parallel RLC is UNDAMPED (zero dissipation)!
Second-Order Initial State Setup at t = 0⁺
To solve 2nd-order ODE x(t) = x_h(t) + x(∞), you need TWO initial conditions:
To find capacitor voltage v_C(t) in Series RLC:
• Initial value: v_C(0⁺) = v_C(0⁻) from continuity.
• Initial derivative: dv_C/dt |_{(0⁺)} = i_C(0⁺) / C = i(0⁺) / C!
Use these two boundary values to solve for integration constants A₁, A₂!
Roots s₁, s₂ are real, distinct, and negative.
x(t) = A₁ · e^{s₁ t} + A₂ · e^{s₂ t} + x(∞)
Waveform: Sluggish non-oscillatory return. Dominated by slower pole (smaller |s|).
x(t) = (A₁ + A₂ · t) · e^{-α t} + x(∞)
FASTEST POSSIBLE RETURN to equilibrium WITHOUT ANY OVERSHOOT!
Preferred in pointer meters, galvanometer suspensions, and servo systems.
x(t) = e^{-α t} · [B₁ · cos(ω_d t) + B₂ · sin(ω_d t)] + x(∞)
= X_m · e^{-α t} · cos(ω_d t - θ) + x(∞)
Waveform: Decaying sinusoidal oscillations bounded by exponential envelopes ±e^{-α t}.
x(t) = C₁ · cos(ω₀ t) + C₂ · sin(ω₀ t) + x(∞)
Zero internal resistance (R=0). Energy oscillates indefinitely back and
forth between capacitor electric field and inductor magnetic field!
Drill 1: Series RLC Step Response (Critically Damped)
Given: V_s = 20 V DC step, R = 20 Ω, L = 1 H, C = 0.01 F (10 mF).
Initial states: i(0⁻) = 0 A, v_C(0⁻) = 0 V.
Given: Current step I_s = 2 A, R = 50 Ω, L = 0.2 H, C = 20 μF.
Initial states: i_L(0⁻) = 0 A, v(0⁻) = 0 V.
Step 2: Boundary Values for Inductor Current i_L(t)
Drill 3: Value of R for Critical Damping (GATE PYQ)
Circuit: L = 4 H and C = 1 μF connected in series with resistor R.
Question: What value of R ensures no oscillatory overshoot?
If the SAME elements are placed in PARALLEL:
R_crit,par = ½ · √(L / C) = ½ · 2000 = 1000 Ω (1 kΩ)
• If R > 1 kΩ: UNDERDAMPED! (Duality inversion trap!)
